literal: The sent message to kings he who delivers, blemish-causing words mouth not reaching, a courageous man.
translation: He who delivers a sent message to other kings must be a man of steadfast courage, whose mouth never utters words that bring blemish or ruin.
modern: அனுப்பப்பட்ட செய்தியை மாற்றரசர்களுக்குச் சொல்பவன், தன் வாயிலிருந்து குற்றம் தரும் சொற்கள் வெளிவராதவாறு காக்கும் அஞ்சாத நெஞ்சமுடையவன் ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essential quality of an envoy when delivering a message to foreign rulers. The envoy must be a person of steadfast courage, referred to as 'vaṉkaṇavaṉ', who does not falter under pressure or threat. Crucially, even in difficult situations, his mouth must never slip to utter 'vaṭumāṟṟam'—faulty, weak, or damaging words that could bring disgrace to his own king. The word 'māṟṟam' is used beautifully in two senses: 'viṭumāṟṟam' refers to the official message sent, while 'vaṭumāṟṟam' refers to flawed words of blame.
